subject: science
notes: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and the smallest planet in the solar system.
Mercury takes about 88 Earth days to complete one orbit of the Sun, so its year is 88 Earth days long.
Mercury rotates slowly, turning once on its axis every 59 Earth days.
Because of the combination of its slow rotation and fast orbit, a full cycle from one sunrise to the next on Mercury takes about 176 Earth days, or two Mercury years.
stem: The student wants to emphasize how unusual the length of a day on Mercury is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system and the closest planet to the Sun.
choices.B: Mercury, the closest planet to the Sun, completes one orbit in about 88 Earth days, so its year is 88 Earth days long.
choices.C: Mercury rotates slowly, turning once on its axis every 59 Earth days.
choices.D: Because Mercury rotates slowly but orbits the Sun quickly, a single sunrise-to-sunrise cycle there lasts about 176 Earth days, or two Mercury years.

explanation.why: The goal is about the length of a day on Mercury, meaning the time from one sunrise to the next. The last note gives the striking fact: that cycle lasts 176 Earth days, which is two of Mercury's years. The key must state that fact; a planet whose day is longer than its year is clearly unusual.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This gives Mercury's size and position, which say nothing about its day.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is about Mercury's year, not its day.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The rotation period is only one part of the story and, on its own, does not show how unusual the day is.
explanation.D: Correct. It gives the length of the sunrise-to-sunrise cycle and notes that it equals two Mercury years, which makes the oddity plain.
